facts.text: I have been trying to improve my skills in data science and programming over the past month.
I have been consuming a lot of educational content over the past month.
I am looking for recommendations on books about machine learning.
I am particularly interested in deep learning.
I plan to start with the book "Deep Learning" by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville.
I have been watching video lectures on statistics by Professor Andrew Ng on MIT OpenCourseWare.
I have already been listening to the Data Science Podcast.
I found the Data Science Podcast episode on natural language processing really insightful.
I am particularly interested in applying NLP to real-world projects.
I worked on a project analyzing customer sentiment using natural language processing.
I have been thinking about working on a project to build a predictive model to forecast stock prices using historical data and news articles.
I think NLP can play a crucial role in analyzing the sentiment and tone of news articles to improve the accuracy of the stock price model.
I plan to collect and preprocess data for the stock price forecasting project.
I plan to use APIs like News API and Quandl to collect historical news articles and stock prices.
For preprocessing, I plan to use NLTK and spaCy to clean and tokenize the text data.
I plan to convert the text data into a numerical representation using TF-IDF or word embeddings.
For sentiment analysis, I am considering using rule-based approaches and machine learning models like Naive Bayes or Support Vector Machines (SVMs).
I am thinking about using deep learning models like convolutional neural networks (CNNs) or recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to analyze sentiment and tone of news articles.
For feature engineering, I plan to extract features like sentiment scores, entity recognition, and topic modeling from the text data.
I plan to experiment with named entity recognition (NER) and part-of-speech (POS) tagging to extract relevant information from the text.
